title: Smt. Kusum Dubey v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Arun Tandon, J.; Harsh Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; liberty to proceed under clause 6.5.
headnote: A consumer disputing the correctness of a bill issued by U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. was held to have a remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was dismissed with that liberty; any interim order stood discharged. The Court did not examine the bill on merits.
facts: Smt. Kusum Dubey invoked the High Court's writ jurisdiction in 2012 against U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. and others. On 30 May 2012 two days were granted to obtain instructions. On 3 July 2012, after instructions were obtained, the Corporation was told to place them on affidavit, with a rejoinder to follow. When a later Division Bench took up the petition on 4 February 2016, the controversy was treated as a dispute over the correctness of a bill issued by the Corporation.

holding_units.holding: If the petitioner disputes the correctness of a bill issued by U.P. Power Corporation Ltd., the remedy is under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ petition is dismissed with that liberty and any interim order stands discharged.
holding_units.flag: Court called clause 6.5 an 'appeal' and did not specify 6.5(a), 6.5(b) or 6.5B.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the disputed electricity bill
not_decided.note: Merits of the bill were not examined; the petitioner was relegated to clause 6.5.
